score_rationale: The module is exceptionally well-structured for a 'consolidated' guide, providing high-level clarity on project-wide standards. D1 is strong due to explicit naming and versioning rules. D2 is lower because while the meta-acceptance criteria (AC-01 to AC-12) are very detailed, they focus on the *structure* of the guidelines rather than the *implementation* of the logic described within the sub-files (e.g., the actual coding rules). D4 is moderate; while it provides some mapping examples, it lacks a 'first-try' implementation walkthrough for a specific guideline. D3 is solid but doesn't fully address concurrency or large-scale drift in the consolidated files themselves.

issues.title: Circular/Self-Referential Acceptance Criteria
issues.why: The ACs in 97-acceptance-criteria.md verify that the files exist and are formatted correctly, but they do not provide GWT tests for the *content* of the guidelines (e.g., 'Given a JSON key with an underscore, When validated, Then it fails').
issues.fix: Add a 'Logic Verification' AC that requires every consolidated rule to have a corresponding negative/positive test case in the linter suite.

issues.title: Missing Worked Examples for Consolidated Format
issues.why: While AC-12 provides a mapping example, there is no example showing how an AI should handle a conflict between a 'Consolidated' rule and a 'Source' rule if drift occurs.
issues.fix: Add a 'Conflict Resolution' example to 00-overview.md explicitly stating that Source ACs always override Consolidated summaries.

issues.title: Stale TODO/Marker Heuristic False Positives
issues.why: The 'Audit Marker Exemption' in 00-overview.md is a manual note rather than a technical contract that an AI coder can implement to avoid linter failures.
issues.fix: Define a specific comment syntax (e.g., // LINTER-IGNORE-TODO) in the coding guidelines to programmatically handle these cases.
